title: Statistics - Measures of Central Tendency and Spread (Basic)
topic: Statistics - Mean, Median, Mode, Range, IQR
subject: Mathematics

questions.question: The test scores of 7 students are: 45, 52, 58, 52, 63, 70, 52. What is the mode of this data set?
questions.explanation: The mode is the value that appears most frequently. 52 appears 3 times, more than any other score (Syllabus 20a).

questions.question: The heights of 5 plants (in cm) are: 10, 12, 14, 16, 18. What is the median height?
questions.explanation: The data is already in order. With 5 values (odd), the median is the middle (3rd) value: 14 cm (Syllabus 20a).

questions.question: The scores of 6 students are: 8, 10, 12, 14, 16, 18. What is the mean score?
questions.explanation: Mean = Sum of values ÷ Number of values = (8+10+12+14+16+18) ÷ 6 = 78 ÷ 6 = 13 (Syllabus 20a).

questions.question: A data set has a lower quartile (Q1) of 25 and an upper quartile (Q3) of 45. What is the interquartile range (IQR)?
questions.explanation: IQR = Q3 - Q1 = 45 - 25 = 20. The IQR measures the spread of the middle 50% of data (Syllabus 20b).

questions.question: The ages of 8 children are: 5, 6, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, 12. What is the lower quartile (Q1)?
questions.explanation: With n=8, Q1 is at position (n+1)/4 = 2.25. Interpolate between 2nd value (6) and 3rd value (6): Q1 = 6 (Syllabus 20b).

questions.question: The prices of 5 items are: $10, $15, $20, $25, $100. Which measure of central tendency is most affected by the extreme value ($100)?
questions.explanation: The mean uses all values in its calculation, so extreme values (outliers) pull it significantly. The median and mode are resistant to outliers (Syllabus 20c).

questions.question: The number of books read by 9 students: 2, 3, 3, 4, 5, 5, 5, 6, 7. What is the median?
questions.explanation: With n=9 (odd), the median is the 5th value in ordered data: 2, 3, 3, 4, [5], 5, 5, 6, 7. Median = 5 (Syllabus 20a).

questions.question: A frequency table shows: Score 1-5: 2 students, 6-10: 5 students, 11-15: 8 students, 16-20: 3 students. Which class interval contains the median?
questions.explanation: Total students = 2+5+8+3 = 18. Median position = (18+1)/2 = 9.5th value. Cumulative frequencies: 2, 7, 15, 18. The 9.5th value falls in the 11-15 interval (Syllabus 20a).

questions.question: The weights (kg) of 7 boxes: 10, 12, 12, 14, 16, 18, 20. What is the upper quartile (Q3)?
questions.explanation: With n=7, Q3 is at position 3(n+1)/4 = 6th value. Ordered data: 10, 12, 12, 14, 16, [18], 20. Q3 = 18 (Syllabus 20b).

questions.question: The daily temperatures (°C) for a week: 22, 24, 24, 25, 26, 28, 30. What is the range?
A data set has a mean of 50 and a standard deviation of 5. If 10 is added to every value in the data set, what is the new mean?
questions.explanation: Adding a constant shifts the central tendency. New mean = Old mean + 10 = 50 + 10 = 60 (Syllabus 20c).

questions.question: A data set has a mean of 50 and a standard deviation of 5. If 10 is added to every value, what is the new standard deviation?
questions.explanation: Adding a constant does not change the spread of data. Standard deviation remains unchanged (Syllabus 20c).

questions.question: A data set consists of 10 values. If every value is multiplied by 3, how does the interquartile range (IQR) change?
questions.explanation: Multiplying all data by a constant scale factor k multiplies all measures of spread (IQR, SD, Range) by |k|. Here k=3 (Syllabus 20b).

questions.question: Two classes have the same mean test score. Class A has SD = 4, Class B has SD = 10. Which class has more consistent scores?
questions.explanation: A smaller standard deviation indicates scores are closer to the mean, meaning more consistent performance. Class A (SD=4) is more consistent (Syllabus 20c).

questions.question: The marks of 5 students: 30, 40, 50, 60, 70. If every mark is multiplied by 2, what is the new median?
questions.explanation: Multiplying all values by 2 also multiplies the median by 2. Original median = 50, new median = 50 × 2 = 100 (Syllabus 20b).
